title: ALMA Hints at the Presence of two Companions in the Disk around HD 100546
question: What are the gas and dust structures of the HD 100546 disk at (sub)mm wavelengths, and do they indicate companions or a protoplanet?

data.sensitivity: continuum rms 0.4 and 0.5 mJy/beam; 19 mJy/beam/channel for CO

what.value: 1.3 and 3.4 mm total flux densities 465±20 and 36±3 mJy (SEST, ATCA)

evidence.quote: yielding a total flux density of 465$\pm$20 and 36$\pm$3 mJy, respectively
which is around 92% of the flux measured with APEX (cite: panic10)

what.value: Disk model, companion mass limit and dust mass used for dust evolution simulations

recipe.method: CLEAN with Briggs weighting after fixvis, self-cal and uvcontsub; moment maps of CO
key_parameters: CO integrated between -12 and +12 km/s of source velocity 5.7 km/s

recipe.method: uvmodelfit elliptical disk to continuum visibilities

recipe.goal: Fit radial structure in visibility domain
recipe.method: Bin deprojected visibilities (10 kλ); grid fit of power-law ring, then Gaussian compact ring plus flat extended ring; chi2 grid with Bayesian errors
key_parameters: fluxes fixed at 0.962 and 0.024 Jy (302 GHz), 1.190 and 0.048 Jy (346 GHz)

recipe.method: Optically thin Mdust = D^2 F / (kappa B(T))
assumptions: kappa=10 cm2/g at 300 GHz, Tdust=60 K; 80 K and 40 K for inner/outer rings

recipe.method: Dust growth/migration models for companion only and companion+protoplanet, compared qualitatively to ALMA
key_parameters: initial size 1 μm, alpha=2e-3, M*=2.4 Msun, dust mass 5e-4 Msun
assumptions: gas-to-dust 100; model extrapolated to 400 AU by power law

evidence.quote: extensive molecular disk (390$\pm$20 AU in radius)
continuum emission is more compact (230$\pm$20 AU in radius)
a total flux density of 0.980 and 1.240 Jy (summing over all flux $\gtrsim$ 3 $\sigma$) at 302 and 346 GHz
position angle (measured East from North) of 146$\pm$4°
there is a zero crossing (null) at 290 k$\lambda$
an outer ring with a width of 75$\pm$3 AU centered at 190$\pm$3 AU
a compact ring with a peak brightness at 26 AU and a FWHM of 21 AU
the total integrated CO flux in these data is 151 Jy km s$^{-1}$

not_stated_but_needed: CLEAN masks, number of iterations and thresholds, cell and image size
Self-calibration solution intervals and number of rounds
Exact visibility-fitting chi2 and Bayesian error procedure
Dust evolution code and numerical set-up (grid, gas surface density profile)
Which execution calibrators apply to which spectral windows
score_reason: Public data and a clear visibility-fitting approach, but imaging/self-cal details and simulation code are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public Cycle 0 data, numeric ring radii and fluxes can be redone via visibility fitting.
